elements.element: No minimum purchase commitment imposed on Customer
elements.evidence: "Customer shall be required to obtain from M&I all of those Services which are included in the Monthly Base Fee"

elements.element: Fees payable only for usage or ordered services
elements.evidence: "a minimum monthly fee (\"Monthly Base Fee\") for certain bundled data processing Services"

elements.element: Commitment limited in duration to the current 12-month term (not the full Term)
elements.evidence: "during the then-current twelve (12) month period, Customer shall be required to obtain from M&I all of those Services"

elements.element: Commitment reducible by Customer on 30 days' notice
elements.evidence: "Customer may, upon 30 days' notice to M&I, reduce or discontinue any Service included in the Monthly Base Fee"

elements.element: Reduction results in a true-up rather than a shortfall penalty
elements.evidence: "the Monthly Base Fee shall be equitably reduced to reflect the resource units no longer used, as a true-up rather than a shortfall penalty"

reasons: All three fallback elements are expressly delivered: the commitment window is cut from the full multi-year Term to the then-current twelve (12) month period, a 30-day reduction/discontinuation right is added, and the consequence is an equitable reduction of the Monthly Base Fee expressly characterised as a true-up rather than a shortfall penalty.
Preferred level is not met and was not the locked target: a minimum monthly fee and an exclusivity obligation to source bundled Services from M&I both survive, so fees are not usage/order-only.

Minimality holds: one short phrase replacement ('during the Term' -> 'during the then-current twelve (12) month period') plus one concise sentence supplying the absent reduction/true-up mechanic; no whole-clause rewrite, no preferred-only language, no new exceptions.

Intent preserved: the Monthly Base Fee construct, volume-based additional charges and Schedule 6.2 scope remain effective; 'Monthly Base Fee', 'Services' and 'Term' remain defined and no dangling mechanic is created.

Note for the rationale rather than as a deviation: the 'Estimated Remaining Value' termination formula still measures months remaining in the full Term using a greater-of multiplier, so a termination-fee exposure beyond the 12-month commitment window persists; this is a separate termination-charge term and does not defeat the fallback on minimum commitment.
